newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DTB futures exchange had temporary overload. [corrected 15:09 gmt]
newsitem.headline: German DTB futures exchange had temporary overload. [corrected 15:09 gmt]

text.p: Germany's DTB electronic equity and debt futures exchange was overloaded for around five minutes after publication of U.S. payroll and unemployment data on Friday, a Deutsche Boerse spokeswoman confirmed.
Some dealers had earlier complained they were unable to see current German options and futures prices on the exchange as a result of the problem.

"The system did not break down, but for about five minutes it was too full," the spokeswoman said by telephone, adding that the problem affected only equity futures (Corrects from "...had affected both equity and debt futures").
The overload is the latest of a number of glitches to have affected German securities trading recently.

Bourse dealings on the cash market were held up for around 30 minutes last month when the exchange's computer system was temporarily unable to provide information either on the DAX index of leading German shares or the individual share prices themselves.
